To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the function of the glucose regulator Cre1 is required for the production of β-lactam antibiotics in the filamentous fungus, Acremonium, which has been used to develop a number of antibiotics.
the function of CRE1 is required for glucose repression of the pcbC gene expression and for the derepressed expression of the cefE gene in the semiprod. strain.
the glucose repressor Cre1 regulates both pcbC and ccefF gene expression in the filamentous fungus, Acremonium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of regulatory mechanisms in filamentous fungi.
the regulation of cephalosporins biosynthesis and the role of the cre1 repressor in this regulation in A. chrysogenum.
the regulation of the biosynthesis genes of cephalosporins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the loss of glucose repression of pcbC gene in the semiproduction strain is caused by a deletion of the cre1 promoter region, and that multiple copies of the intact cre1 gene restore the glucose repression.
the loss of CRE1 function is responsible for the derepression of cephalosporins biosynthesis in the improved strain.
the semiproducers have a mutation in a regulatory gene, which is responsible for the deregulation of the glucose repression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of glucose repression in Acremonium strains correlates with the loss of the CRE1 function and that this loss can be compensated by multiple copies of cre1.
the pcbC gene is regulated by the CRE1 repressor and the cefE gene is regulated by both CRE1 and the CRE1 repressible CRE2 repressor.
we were able to show that the glucose repression of the pcbC gene is dependent on the presence of the cre1 protein and that this repression can be restored by multiple copies of this gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glucose repressor Cre1 is involved in regulation of the pcb C gene expression, and that the pcb C and cef EF genes are not coordinately regulated.

a strain with enhanced cephamycin C production shows deregulation of the glucose repression system, and that this deregulation can be reverted by the addition of multiple copies of the glucose repressors gene.
the glucose repression mechanism is a target for strain improvement in the filamentous fungus.
